races.name: Virgin Bet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Swing Vote
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford runner who is well-suited to soft Goodwood over a mile (3 course starts at this trip), with the hood retained and William Buick booked; 74 days off the track is the only mild concern, but the form figures show consistency in competitive handicaps at this venue.

runners_data.name: Godwinson
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's hold-up specialist has course form but his recent string — 10th, 18th, 10th, 12th, 14th at Goodwood — paints a bleak picture of a horse struggling badly in this grade; soft going is no concern but his win record here belies a persistent tendency to disappoint on the day.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old races from the back and has soft-ground and Goodwood form to point to — notably a win here on Good to Firm and a recent Goodwood victory 16 days ago (LR:16d) that makes him fresher than most; Kaiya Fraser takes over and the horse's profile is the most compelling of the hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Real Gain
runners_data.note: Hamad Al Jehani's six-year-old carries a pacemaking headgear flag (hg:p) and is a genuine prominent racer with positive course form at the mile trip; Harry Vigors (5) claims 5lbs which is a meaningful weight relief, though the recent form reading (00-458) tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Oliver Show
runners_data.note: George Boughey's gelding carries tongue tie and a hood, is a prominent-style runner whose best form has come at shorter than a mile, and his recent mile runs at Goodwood (14th) suggest the trip stretches him on soft ground; Loughnane rides in a yard that has had a productive recent spell (T14: 5/32).

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's eight-year-old ran only yesterday (LR:1d) which is an unusually tight turnaround and represents a significant physical question on soft ground; the ⚠ flag for fading in finishes compounds the concern, and while he has soft-going form, the combination of age, quick return, and finishing pattern makes him the most operationally suspect runner.

runners_data.name: Rainbow Nebula
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's four-year-old has contested mainly ten-furlong races and drops back to a mile here — a genuine prominent runner whose natural position cannot be filled in this crowded pace scenario, meaning it will be forced to race out of role in midfield; the trip shortening is a further uncertainty and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) rightly tempers expectation.

runners_data.name: Masked Warrior
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the race, giving Cieren Fallon full control of the tempo from the off; soft-ground form exists (three places in six soft-ground runs) and the yard is firing (T14: 6/45), making him the pivotal horse around whom the entire race shape is built.

runners_data.name: Drifts Away
runners_data.note: T J Kent's five-year-old has excellent course form — two Goodwood wins in the last five — and a prominent style well-suited to sitting just off Masked Warrior; soft-going form is modest (1W1P from 15 similar-going runs) but the yard's low runner frequency (T14: 1/7) and the horse's mile course record make this a credible each-way profile.

runners_data.name: Silca Bay
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer — two Goodwood wins from eight course starts — but the crowded pace picture means it is likely to be shuffled back into midfield rather than getting its preferred position; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) accurately reflects that racing out of role on soft ground materially reduces its winning prospects despite the course record.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's four-year-old has strong Goodwood form (2nd, 1st, 2nd in last three course starts) and is arguably the best-credentialled horse in the race on raw recent form, but as a natural prominent type forced into midfield by the crowded pace scenario, it faces a positional compromise; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) and Clifford Lee partnership in a Burke yard running at high volume (T14: 10/45) means the talent is there but the shape may not deliver it.

races.paceDynamic: Masked Warrior is the confirmed lone front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Cieren Fallon can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground around Goodwood's undulating mile. The pace will be honest but not pressured, meaning the tempo is set entirely on Masked Warrior's terms — likely enough to string the field out on soft going without burning himself up. Swing Vote, Real Gain, Oliver Show, and Drifts Away will hunt prominent positions behind the leader, creating a tight, compact early order, while Godwinson, Principality, and Rhoscolyn settle at the rear as true hold-up types. This field contains more prominent-minded horses than can all secure their natural position — Silca Bay and Inspired are genuine prominent types who will be shuffled into midfield, compromising their chances in any shape that relies on them stalking from close range. The race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile: with a controlled, uncontested pace on soft ground, horses who can travel close to Masked Warrior and challenge from two furlongs out carry the clearest tactical advantage, while pure closers will need significant late momentum that a steady pace on soft Goodwood may not generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Masked Warrior dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the horses just off the pace get first run turning for home.
scenarios.body: Masked Warrior's rhythm goes unchallenged through the first half, and horses like Swing Vote and Drifts Away — travelling close throughout — strike from two out before hold-up types can close the gap on softened ground; soft Goodwood historically rewards those who race forward and finish through the line rather than launching late runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the front group ties up inside the final furlong, leaving a genuine gap for closers.
scenarios.body: Principality, who has proven soft-ground form at Goodwood and a recent winning run, would be the prime beneficiary of any genuine fade from the pace-setters; Godwinson has the style and course form but has been consistently disappointing in this grade, limiting confidence in a hold-up surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Masked Warrior gets an entirely uncontested, near-walk early pace on soft ground and the field settles into a false race before a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A very slow pace on soft Goodwood can paradoxically suit the leader if no one is willing to challenge — Masked Warrior's Haggas yard is in strong form (T14: 6/45) and the horse has course-and-distance form; in a sprint finish on softened ground, class and freshness from the front can be decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely searching and the front-rank horses are all compromised, allowing a horse delivered from midfield to pick them off.
scenarios.body: Rainbow Nebula and Inspired are true prominent types pushed into midfield by the field's crowded pace positions, meaning their redistribution significantly compromises this scenario — the midfield contingent is not comprised of natural hold-up horses building up a head of steam, so this shape is the least likely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Rhoscolyn ran yesterday (LR:1d) — watch for any sign of distress or below-par movement in the paddock before committing any assessment, as the turnaround on soft ground for an eight-year-old is highly unusual and potentially significant.

Principality is the most credible hold-up threat — watch whether Kaiya Fraser gives it a patient, wide ride turning in, as a clear run from two out on soft Goodwood could see it sprint past tired front-runners given its recent winning form here.

Silca Bay and Inspired are both natural prominent types who cannot hold their preferred positions — watch whether either jockey (Carmichael or Lee) elects to push forward aggressively from the stalls, which would increase early pace and compress Masked Warrior's control of the race.

Masked Warrior's ability to control the pace entirely depends on no one challenging — watch the early break from Real Gain and Swing Vote, as either pushing forward assertively could turn a controlled lead into a contested one and fundamentally change the race shape.

Drifts Away's two Goodwood wins from recent form suggest course affinity that can be underestimated in the market — watch whether Ray Dawson positions it within two lengths of Masked Warrior at halfway, as that stalking role on this course has repeatedly proved the winning position.

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Callum Rodriguez and Jack Channon, with two placed efforts at Goodwood on fast ground but limited impact on similar going (2/15 record); dropping back to 6f suits more than 7f but needs a collapsing pace to get involved from the rear.

runners_data.name: Fandom
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 5-year-old is a natural prominent racer with a solid course record at Goodwood (multiple runs, three recent 6f starts here); the going is fine but he wants to be on Ardisia's girths from the off, and with several rivals wanting the same slot he must assert early.

runners_data.name: Ardisia
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner for Oisin Murphy and Hugo Palmer — this is an out-of-role style flag since Ardisia is listed P rather than L by default, but she is the lone pace-setter here and sets the entire tempo; soft going tested recently with placed efforts, and her ability to control from the front is the pivot of the whole race.

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners this David O'Meara hold-up 5-year-old who won on soft ground at Goodwood (1/6f/SOF in hist) and has an excellent 7/15 sim-going record — the best soft-ground fit in the field; needs the pace to collapse but has the profile for that scenario.

runners_data.name: Lakers
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's 4-year-old was off 135 days (longest absence in the race) and returns from a break with a win over 6f at Staines and placed efforts; David Egan rides and he wants to be prominent, but fitness after such a long lay-off on soft ground is the key question.

runners_data.name: Fast Track Harry
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's 4-year-old runs in a tongue-piece and is a prominent type with one win and one place from 14 similar-going starts; Billy Loughnane has been busy for Cox lately (5 runs, 5 wins from 24), but recent form figures (770020) show he is out of form and the soft ground may not bring out his best.

runners_data.name: Flash Harry
runners_data.note: Cox's second string — Rossa Ryan partners this 4-year-old who has a poor recent record (0-6090) and has finished out of the frame on both soft-ground starts; prominent in style but the form simply does not warrant much confidence, and the yard's T14 split between two runners dilutes trainer focus.

runners_data.name: Purosangue
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark on Robert Cowell's 5-year-old who has placed at Goodwood on fast ground but has a stronger record at 5f than 6f; the soft going (7/15 sim-going starts) is not a barrier, but hold-up style in a race with a controlled pace is a tactical disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Havana Hurricane
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 3-year-old runs in a hood for the first time and is a hold-up type with just one comparable soft-ground start; Charles Bishop rides, and the age and weight concessions from older rivals on soft ground look significant, though a first-time hood effect is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 8-year-old won at Goodwood over this exact course and distance (1/6f/GOO) and has placed twice on similar going; Billy Garritty is a capable claimer and the horse wants to be in second or third — his consistency and local course knowledge make him a solid fit for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Rapper's Delight
runners_data.note: George Wood rides this 4-year-old who has two recent placed efforts at 5f on good-to-firm; a genuine prominent type by nature but, with this field stacked with P-style horses, he is unlikely to secure his preferred berth — the visor goes on and the form at 6f on soft is unproven, meaning his pace credentials are diluted in practice here.

runners_data.name: Jungle Drums
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's 4-year-old won over 6f at Staines on standard ground and placed at Goodwood; a true hold-up horse who has been pushed into a midfield mapping by volume — William Carver rides and his soft-ground record (5/15) is respectable, but the redistribution means he will race further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' 4-year-old has placed in three of his last five over 6f at Goodwood and handles soft going; by inclination a front-of-the-pace type, but the density of prominent runners means he is mapped to midfield and Finley Marsh will need to be clever early — his natural position is foreclosed before the stalls open.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Chief
runners_data.note: Heather Main's 5-year-old ran just yesterday (1d since last run — shortest interval in the race) and has a poor recent string (-30998); Luke Morris rides but the back-to-back scheduling, a soft-going record of just 1 from 15, and drifting form make him very hard to recommend, hold-up style notwithstanding.

runners_data.name: Purest Time
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' 6-year-old won at Goodwood over 6f (1/6f/GOO in hist) but recent figures (071790) are poor; David Probert partners a natural hold-up horse who has been remapped due to field overcrowding at the rear — the form and going record (2/15 on sim-going) offer limited encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Ardisia is the confirmed front-runner and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a field of 15, she is likely to dictate on a comfortable, sustainable gallop from stall to home bend — particularly significant on Goodwood's flat 6f where a controlled leader rarely gets run down without significant pressure. The soft ground will emphasise stamina over raw speed, stretching the field and making position off the bend crucial; horses that can sit just behind Ardisia without expending early energy will be best placed to pounce. Fandom, Lakers, Fast Track Harry, Flash Harry and Strike Red all have prominent claims, but with multiple genuine prominent types competing for a handful of seats, Rapper's Delight and Sudden Flight — both true P-style horses — are displaced to midfield in the map and may not secure their natural berth. This shape firmly favours horses that can race in second or third on a moderate pace and produce a sustained late effort, with genuine hold-up closers at a disadvantage unless the pace collapses entirely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ardisia Controls, Prominents Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ardisia dictates a moderate tempo on soft ground and the race is set up for those tucked just behind her.
scenarios.body: Ardisia sets a civilised pace over Goodwood's flat 6f, and the horses immediately off her heels enjoy the perfect slingshot into the straight; the soft going rewards those who conserve energy in the first three furlongs and sprint late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Ups Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Ardisia's tempo is genuinely slow and the field concertinas, allowing true hold-up horses to thread through on the run-in.
scenarios.body: A dawdle would compress the field into the final 2f and give closers a clear run at an unextended leader; genuine hold-up horses who have settled well off a slow gallop can pick up powerfully through a tiring pack on soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Builds, Soft Ground Saps Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more pressured than expected and Ardisia ties up approaching the straight, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: Multiple prominent types angling for position early would create enough friction to raise the tempo, and the soft ground would punish those who race freely; a horse with a strong late turn of foot from just off the pace would benefit most as the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Horses Hit Front
scenarios.trigger: If Rapper's Delight or Sudden Flight manage to reclaim their natural prominent positions and force the issue on soft ground.
scenarios.body: In a scenario where these displaced front-runners scramble to their preferred spots and set a genuine gallop, the race becomes a stamina test over 6f on soft; their true style would serve them well if they achieve it, but the map suggests they are unlikely to get there uncontested.

watchPoints.text: Ardisia (Oisin Murphy) sets the entire pace dynamic — watch her stall behaviour and whether she is allowed to stride on or is restrained; any flicker of pressure in the first furlong from Fandom or Strike Red would fundamentally alter the race shape.

Lakers (David Egan) is 135 days absent and returns on soft ground — if she misses the kick or is sluggish early the long break may catch her out, but a fluent exit would put her right in the pivotal position just behind the leader.

Rapper's Delight and Sudden Flight are genuine prominent types who cannot both get their preferred position with Ardisia, Fandom, Lakers, Fast Track Harry, Flash Harry and Strike Red all wanting the same real estate — watch for crowding and bumping in the opening furlong that could compromise multiple runners.
Zoulu Chief (Luke Morris) ran just yesterday — monitor his markets move and pre-race demeanour; back-to-back runs on soft ground for a horse in poor form is a stable confidence signal worth tracking.

Havana Hurricane wears a hood for the first time — first-time headgear on a young 3-year-old in a competitive 15-runner handicap on soft ground can produce unpredictable early behaviour, and her starting position and reaction to the gates should be watched closely.

races.name: Virgin Bet Prestige Fillies' Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Aperoll
runners_data.note: Hannon-trained 2yo with two runs at this course and distance (1st and 3rd), but faces intense competition for the lead from Coaxed and Bayside View; burning energy contesting the front on Soft ground is a real stamina risk over 7f.

runners_data.name: Apollo's Comet
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 120 alongside Coaxed, Mrs Harrington's filly won over this exact course and distance last time and has course form at the G3 level; 73 days off is the query but her profile is perfectly suited to a truly-run race that tests stamina.

runners_data.name: Bayside View
runners_data.note: Murphy takes the ride on this Bell-trained front-runner who has placed in all three Goodwood starts including over 7f; she wants to lead but will be squeezed for that role by Coaxed and Aperoll, meaning she may end up racing prominently at a cost.

runners_data.name: Coaxed
runners_data.note: Buick and Gosden send out the unbeaten Coaxed on just her second career start, rated 120 off a single Sandown win; she is entered as a front-runner and with the top stable combination behind her, she is the key pace-setter — but whether she is ready for a contested soft-ground 7f Group 3 on race two is the crucial question.

runners_data.name: Eabha
runners_data.note: Lightly raced but in fine form — three wins from five including back-to-back 7f wins at Goodwood — and only 15 days since last run suggests a fit, in-form filly; she wants to race prominently and her soft-going record (1W from 2 in similar conditions) is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Light Of Dawn
runners_data.note: Burke's filly has an excellent record in soft ground (1W 2P from 3 soft runs) and steps up from 6f to 7f, which the Goodwood track should suit; Clifford Lee rides for the high-volume Burke yard (10/45 in 14 days) and this is a filly on the upgrade.

runners_data.name: Martinet
runners_data.note: Prescott sends out this front-runner who showed improvement on her last two starts winning at Goodwood, but racing prominently against four other keen pace-makers on Soft is a stern stamina test; Luke Morris will need luck in running if she gets shuffled back.

runners_data.name: Nuit d'Eclair
runners_data.note: De Foy's filly has placed over this C&D twice in three runs including a 2nd last time at Goodwood, suggesting strong course affinity; OR 100 and happy to race prominently off a genuine pace, she could prove an each-way banker if the leaders fade on the testing ground.

runners_data.name: Redline
runners_data.note: Johnston's unbeaten filly (2-from-2, both at Goodwood) stretches in trip from 6f to 7f and has been off 55 days; she wants to lead but faces a wall of pace rivals, and the soft ground over the longer 7f journey on a return from absence adds layers of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Siena Storm
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly drops back from a winning 8f run at Goodwood to 7f, making her the most natural hold-up runner in the race; soft ground holds no fears and she could benefit most if the pace truly implodes, though the step down in trip means she is reliant on a strong gallop to set up her finishing run.

races.paceDynamic: Five front-runners — Coaxed, Aperoll, Bayside View, Martinet, and Redline — all want the same piece of real estate at Goodwood's 7f start, guaranteeing a contested, strong gallop from the off on Soft ground that will stretch stamina to its limit. Coaxed (Buick/Gosden) is likely to assert quickest and command the rail, with Aperoll and Bayside View forced to race prominently at pace rather than dictating as they might prefer, while Martinet and Redline face a squeeze for position that will cost energy. The resulting end-to-end tempo on soft ground plays directly into the hands of horses tracking off the pace in third to fifth position, allowing them to conserve and produce a sustained late run without being buried in traffic. Prominent-to-midfield types with proven soft-ground stamina over 7f — particularly Apollo's Comet, Nuit d'Eclair, and Light Of Dawn — are most favoured by this shape, as the contested lead will likely burn out the front-running contingent before the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Field
scenarios.trigger: If Coaxed and Aperoll trade blows up front and the pace duly collapses the leaders in the straight on soft ground
scenarios.body: The strong pace set by multiple leaders on Soft going saps those at the front two furlongs out, leaving the race to those who tracked in fourth to sixth; Apollo's Comet and Nuit d'Eclair, both comfortable on this course and in this going, have the class and position to sweep past a strung-out field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Sees Coaxed Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Coaxed proves superior in class, settles beautifully under Buick and finds more in the straight than rivals can match
scenarios.body: Buick's horsemanship could see Coaxed control the tempo rather than burn herself out, producing a measured lead that turns the race into a test of raw quality; as the only runner with an OR of 120 on a single start, her ceiling is the unknown — and potentially far above this field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweep Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly ferocious and even prominent horses weaken, leaving the race to those held up
scenarios.body: Siena Storm, who won over 8f at Goodwood and is dropped back in trip, makes most appeal as a hold-up runner if the leaders implode completely; Light Of Dawn's two soft-ground runs show strong form and she could motor home down the outside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Pace Blunts Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves surprisingly honest rather than suicidal and a prominent horse times the run perfectly
scenarios.body: Eabha has the course form and the fitness (15 days since last run) to sit handy and produce a clean finish if the race is not truly run; Bayside View with Murphy aboard could recover from the early scramble and stick on for a place.

watchPoints.text: Coaxed and Aperoll are on a collision course for the lead — watch the first two furlongs to see who blinks; if neither concedes, the early burn rate on Soft ground could compromise both their winning chances.
Redline has been absent 55 days and is unproven beyond 6f — her two wins came here at Goodwood but the longer trip, testing ground, and stiff pace test on return from a break make her vulnerable.
Apollo's Comet is 73 days off the track and her trainer T14 strike rate of 2/30 is modest — if ring rustiness shows in the first furlong, Loughnane may lose the prominent pitch she needs.

Siena Storm is the sole hold-up runner and her finishing kick depends entirely on the pace being genuinely strong — if Buick produces a mesmerising front-running display from Coaxed that controls the tempo, Siena Storm's race is over before the straight.

Light Of Dawn steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time but has shown soft-ground class on two previous occasions; watch where Clifford Lee positions her in the first half-mile — if she travels smoothly in midfield, she is one of the most likely beneficiaries of the contested pace scenario.

races.name: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Echalar
runners_data.note: Ran well to win over 10f at Goodwood last time, giving trainer Ian Williams a timely boost, but this horse's natural running style is from the rear; with the field crowded at the back, Billy Loughnane may find it hard to secure that position, and style-fit pressure reduces its chance in this shape — soft-ground form on the course is limited (0W0P in similar going).|

runners_data.name: Gloryous
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's front-runner has come in off just four days since last running and holds a win over 12f at Salisbury plus placed form over 12f at Goodwood; William Carson takes the ride and this horse will set out to make every yard — soft going (1W from 15 similar-going runs) is the concern, but with Itica for company it can run its race.|

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: William Haggas has placed this lightly raced three-year-old in a selling stakes having won over 8f at Goodwood; Cieren Fallon rides with the horse wearing a tongue strap, stepping up significantly in trip to 1m3f for the first time — the single soft-going run (11th over 10f on soft) does not inspire confidence, and trip doubt is real.|

runners_data.name: Ohara
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old has placed form over 12f at Goodwood (2nd) and stays this trip, but is running in this competitive context with seven-pound claimer Oliver Carmichael; a natural hold-up runner by inclination, it will find its back-of-field position squeezed by the number of similar types and limited soft-going wins (1W1P from 11 runs) temper enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Sudbury Hill
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's progressive three-year-old has won twice over 10f at Goodwood (including a recent win) and holds strong course form; Callum Rodriguez takes the ride, and wearing a hood the horse has finished placed at this track in similar conditions — its front-foot racing style suits a genuinely run race and course knowledge is a clear asset.|

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: David O'Meara sends this three-year-old in off just one day since its last run — highly unusual and worth flagging; Daniel Tudhope rides a horse that has won on soft over 9f and placed over 12f on soft recently, though by nature it wants to race from the back and finds its preferred position compressed by the field's hold-up-heavy profile.|

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old has won over 12f at Goodwood and finished placed in a soft-ground contest over 10f; Clifford Lee rides this horse which carries the prominent tag and has the form to be competitive from a tracking position — five runs in similar going (1W3P) suggest it handles conditions, and its style is best suited to this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Itica
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old is the second confirmed front-runner under Oisin Murphy; form figures of 02-56 are modest and its Goodwood experience is limited, with most form on the all-weather at Sandown — it will push Gloryous for the early lead but whether it can sustain that into soft ground over 1m3f is the obvious question, and OR71 is the lowest in this field.|

races.paceDynamic: Gloryous and Itica are confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead over 1m3f on soft ground at Goodwood, creating a genuine and honest gallop from the outset rather than a dawdle. With both horses committed to making the pace, the race will be run at a consistent tempo through the first half, stretching the field before the final turn and putting a premium on stamina and efficiency of movement in testing conditions. Dunkeld Dreamer will press close behind the two leaders, with Sudbury Hill and Lorca's Waltz likely to settle in behind that trio, while Echalar, Ohara, and Unchartedterritory — all genuine hold-up types — find themselves operating closer to the pace than their natural style dictates because this field has more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear. This race shape favours a prominent or patient hold-up runner with proven soft-ground stamina who can exploit a genuinely run gallop set by Gloryous and Itica — a closer making ground through the final quarter mile is the most favoured profile, provided it is not one of the horses artificially pushed up from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gloryous and Itica set an honest gallop that drains the field on soft ground, leaving a genuine test of stamina from the 4f pole home.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners push each other along through soft ground, creating a true test that exposes any horse lacking stamina or soft-ground experience, and a prominent runner with proven staying ability can reel them in late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Gloryous settles into a rhythm and Itica cannot sustain the pace, allowing one horse to control the gallop from a manageable position.
scenarios.body: With only one genuine front-runner able to sustain their position, the lead horse sets an economical pace that suits its own stamina profile and the horse in behind gets a soft lead to track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace between Gloryous and Itica burns sufficiently hot that the entire field is softened, leaving a late burst possible from the back.
scenarios.body: A truly run race on soft ground can create the conditions for a strong finisher, but this scenario depends on one of the redistributed hold-up horses actually operating from further back than their mapped position suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Tempo, Punter's Race
scenarios.trigger: If neither Gloryous nor Itica sustains the pace and the gallop becomes muddled or irregular, turning the race into a sprint for home.
scenarios.body: A collapse in tempo on soft ground suits the horse able to quicken from a prominent position who has been tracking without expending energy, though form becomes difficult to weigh in a muddled race.

watchPoints.text: Unchartedterritory runs off just one day since its last race — connections must have a specific reason for this quick turnaround, whether that is a race target or a fitness concern, and punters should probe this before betting.

Gloryous and Itica will contest the early lead and the pace between them on soft ground could burn out both front-runners before the home turn — if either weakens rapidly, the race becomes very open for the prominent trackers.

Lorca's Waltz steps up dramatically in trip from 8f to 1m3f in soft going having finished 11th on its only soft-ground start — the combination of unproven stamina and testing conditions represents a notable risk.

Dunkeld Dreamer has strong recent course form (1W3P at Goodwood) and K.R. Burke's yard has had 10 runners in the last 14 days — the trainer is in form and this horse's prominent style maps neatly onto the race shape created by the two front-runners.

Sudbury Hill has won twice at Goodwood over 10f and wears a hood — any horse showing strong track affinity in selling-grade company on soft ground deserves respect as the front-runners press each other into fatigue.

races.name: City Of Chichester Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Has placed at this course over 2m and 2m4f, handled soft ground once in five attempts (one place), and Sir Mark Prescott's 6-from-16 stable form is solid; races prominently and will be squeezed for position in a crowded pace bracket — needs a smooth passage to be effective.

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride for a stable that has been modest in form (2/9 last 14 days); recent record shows a sole win at Goodwood in January over 2m, but has twice finished ninth at this course this season — likely to be ridden prominently but will struggle to assert in a busy early phase.

runners_data.name: Blazeon Five
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old genuine hold-up horse with two wins in soft or similar conditions in his recent history and multiple places; Alan King's runner arrives fresh (64 days off) which can suit stayers, and his style means he will bypass the early scrimmage entirely — the most naturally positioned horse for a strongly-run race.

runners_data.name: Squire Danagher
runners_data.note: Has winning recent form, including a Goodwood handicap success over 14f, and handles soft ground with a place from three similar-going runs; races prominently and Emma Lavelle's yard is out of form (0/7 last 14 days), but a horse who relaxes well off the pace could be dangerous if the front-runners soften each other up.

runners_data.name: Senor Cortez
runners_data.note: Has won three of his last three races, all on faster surfaces at Sandown and Nottingham, and arrives on a sharply upward curve; Billy Loughnane is a strong booking and the horse races prominently, but this is his first soft-ground start in this form cycle and the step to 2m at Goodwood is a significant test of his stamina ceiling.

runners_data.name: Moon Over Miami
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's runner has a win over 2m at Goodwood on his card and handles soft ground (1W1P from two soft runs); he is a natural prominent racer but the congested pace map means he is unlikely to get his preferred early position — his chance is tempered by racing against his instincts in a field with more pace than it can accommodate.

runners_data.name: Marnier
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with two placed efforts on soft-ish ground and multiple Goodwood appearances; Gary & Josh Moore's yard has been modest (2/25, no wins in 14 days) but the horse's style suits a strongly-run race perfectly, and his recent sixth at Goodwood over 2m shows the trip and track are no obstacle.

runners_data.name: Personal Best
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed front-runners, with two wins and consistent form at Goodwood including a 14f win here; soft ground is fine (2W4P from 13 efforts on similar going) and Rob Hornby rides, but leading over 2m in soft with a rival pressing throughout will ask serious stamina questions of a horse rated only 82.

runners_data.name: Maxident
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter, consistent in soft conditions (1W7P from 15 runs, remarkable place record), and David Egan is an astute jockey who may try to dictate rather than duel; Kevin Philippart De Foy's yard is in modest form (2/10), but Maxident's tenacity and soft-ground record make him the more durable front-runner of the two.

runners_data.name: Premiere Ligne
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse arriving on a sequence of poor efforts — 6th, 7th, 6th, 9th, 15th — including two last-place finishes in soft ground; Oisin Murphy's booking is the sole positive angle, but the form and headgear note (tongue strap) suggest a horse that has not fired recently and is a significant risk to disappoint again.

runners_data.name: Knight Templar
runners_data.note: Has placed three times and won once at Goodwood, with solid placed form over shorter trips; a natural prominent racer who is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal given the crowded pace positions, and with a style fit of 0.93 his chance is materially discounted — David Probert must find a way to place him without his natural early berth.

races.paceDynamic: Personal Best and Maxident are the two confirmed front-runners and will battle for the lead from the off over this 2m trip on soft ground at Goodwood, creating a genuinely contested early gallop that is unlikely to ease. With Synergism, Bahadur, Squire Danagher, and Senor Cortez all naturally prominent, the pace bracket is heavily congested, meaning the early fractions should be honest rather than dawdling — soft ground will only amplify the stamina test this imposes. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions; Personal Best and Maxident are most likely to actually lead, with Senor Cortez and Synergism best-placed among the prominent pack to settle just behind, while Moon Over Miami and Knight Templar — both natural prominent racers — are likely to be shuffled back against their instincts. A contested, honest pace on soft ground over 2m is a setup that classically rewards the relaxed, well-stayinghold-up or deep-midfield horse who can conserve energy before picking off a tiring field in the straight, making that profile the primary tactical beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stayers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Personal Best and Maxident push each other along from the start, draining the prominent pack through soft ground before the straight.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop set by the two front-runners saps the legs of those racing keenly in behind, leaving the race to horses who have settled and conserved energy; the soft going amplifies the stamina test and makes it nearly impossible for a prominent horse to repel a fresh closer. Blazeon Five and Marnier, both genuine hold-up types with strong soft-ground form, are ideally positioned to pick off the tiring leaders in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners gains a decisive early advantage and the field settles into a steady, controlled rhythm rather than a true battle for the lead.
scenarios.body: With less internal pressure than expected, a front-runner can find a rhythm and husband stamina reserves through the soft, emerging from the final turn with enough left to hold on; Personal Best has a strong recent record over this type of trip and course, and Maxident's consistent placing record in similar conditions makes both viable under this shape. The soft ground still demands a genuine stayer, so neither can coast, but an uncontested lead is transformative over 2m.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely even and no single horse is destroyed, allowing a prominent horse racing just behind the leaders to produce a turn-of-foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: Senor Cortez arrives in career-best form having won three consecutive races and could be well-placed tracking the pace before asserting; Squire Danagher, who has course form and recent winning handicap form, could also capitalise if allowed to settle just off the leaders rather than being crowded out. This scenario is somewhat dampened by the soft ground placing a premium on stamina over acceleration, limiting the scope for a sharp pick-up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners collapse quickly, creating a sprint-like finish from deep in the straight that suits only the fastest finishers coming from far back.
scenarios.body: Premiere Ligne or Blazeon Five could theoretically fly home if the race falls perfectly, but both are being asked to overcome slow early positions and produce dramatic late runs, which is a low-probability combination over soft 2m at Goodwood. This scenario requires an unlikely collapse of the entire prominent group simultaneously, making it the least plausible shape in this field.

watchPoints.text: Personal Best and Maxident — watch how aggressively both go for the early lead; if they duel hard from the start on soft ground over 2m, neither may have enough left to hold on in the final two furlongs, and the entire complexion of the race changes.

Senor Cortez — his three-timer comes on faster ground and he has never raced on soft in this form; if he shows any sign of discomfort in the going early on, his chance evaporates rapidly over this stamina-sapping trip.

Knight Templar and Moon Over Miami — both natural prominent horses who may be shuffled back into unfamiliar positions at the start; watch whether either can work into a forward berth or whether they are trapped in midfield traffic, which would materially reduce their chance.

Blazeon Five — freshness (64 days off) can be a positive for stayers, and Alan King's horse has won fresh before; watch his early positioning from Rossa Ryan — if he settles smoothly in rear he is ideally set up for the closing stages.

Premiere Ligne with Oisin Murphy — an otherwise out-of-form hold-up horse getting an elite jockey booking; watch whether Murphy opts for an unusually forward ride to counter the horse's losing streak, which would signal a tactical reversal worth noting.

races.name: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: A Major Payne
runners_data.note: Course specialist with four of his last five runs at Goodwood including two wins over this exact 10f trip; sits prominent naturally and Oisin Murphy's booking is a strong positive, though a field this competitive may force him wider than ideal.|

runners_data.name: War Hawk
runners_data.note: Consistent at Goodwood but has not won in five course attempts at this track; soft going is within range but his sim-going record (1W from 15 runs) offers little confidence he will find extra when it matters.|

runners_data.name: Thinthread
runners_data.note: Returned a well-beaten tenth on his most recent Goodwood start and has been inconsistent; George Baker's runner holds a Stamford win over 10f but the step back to soft ground at Goodwood is a concern given a modest similar-going record.|

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 10f on soft ground is the standout going qualification in this field; naturally inclined to race from the rear and Daniel Tudhope will look to exploit a pace collapse, making him one of the most naturally suited to how this race is expected to unfold.|

runners_data.name: First Ambition
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose recent form reads poorly — six, nineteen, seven in his last three soft-ground runs — and even if he secures the lead, his record suggests he may struggle to sustain it under these conditions against this level.|

runners_data.name: Bearish
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up in trip having been very lightly campaigned; won over 8f at Goodwood on good but his sole soft-ground run was a distant thirteenth, making the going switch a significant unknown against older, more proven rivals.|

runners_data.name: Alcaraz
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has placed on soft twice in his last four runs over this trip and whose most recent course run ended in a distant fourteenth; David Egan rides a horse who, when conditions suit, has genuine finishing speed but needs things to go right from midfield.|

runners_data.name: Due To Henry
runners_data.note: Ran a solid third on soft over 10f most recently and is a natural prominent racer — the note here is that his preferred berth will be contested by several others, so Charles Bishop may find him further back than he'd like, which partially limits his chance.|

runners_data.name: Brigid's Well
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old filly has not shown the form on soft or at Goodwood that would make her a force here; headgear (tongue-tie, pads) suggests she needs assistance to settle, and her recent record of 7-6-10-5-4 underlines her inconsistency.|

runners_data.name: Si Grass
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at Stamford and shaped with promise early in his career, but his natural front-running instincts will be crowded out in this field; Charlie Johnston's runner, stepping from 8f to 10f for the first time, faces a trip and pace-shape that may not suit.|

runners_data.name: Lavender Gold
runners_data.note: The other confirmed pace-setter; won over 10f on soft last time at Stamford which is a positive going qualification, but stepping into handicap company at Goodwood over a longer trip and having to share the front against First Ambition significantly raises the difficulty.|

races.paceDynamic: First Ambition and Lavender Gold are the two confirmed front-runners in this 11-runner 1m2f Goodwood handicap on soft ground, and with both likely to press for the early lead, this race will be run at an honest, competitive gallop from the outset — neither horse has the class to dominate and ease the pace. The soft ground at Goodwood will amplify the energy cost of that early battle, meaning the leaders are likely to be fully cooked by the straight, setting up a race that rewards horses who can travel smoothly in behind and quicken through tired rivals. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural berth: A Major Payne, War Hawk, Thinthread, and Bearish all want to race close to the pace, meaning Si Grass and Due To Henry — genuine prominent racers — are redistributed to midfield positions they would not naturally seek. Given contested early fractions on soft ground over 1m2f, hold-up and midfield runners who settle and stay on under the conditions are favoured, with truly prominent horses who can handle being slightly held up (rather than those who need to lead) best placed to benefit as the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If First Ambition and Lavender Gold set a genuinely taxing early gallop on soft ground that drains the prominent pack.
scenarios.body: The two leaders fight for supremacy and burn through their stamina reserves by halfway, leaving the race wide open in the final three furlongs for those who settled behind; soft ground amplifies the pace collapse and rewards genuine stayers who travelled within themselves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivors Grind On
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not truly punishing, allowing prominent horses that settle slightly off the leaders to grind out the finish.
scenarios.body: A Major Payne or Bearish, close enough to see what happens but not exposed by the fractions, use their experience and course form to repel closers in a steadier final furlong; soft ground suits those with a high cruising speed rather than a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft-Ground Stayer Scores
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses so thoroughly that only those with genuine soft-ground stamina and tactical patience can sustain a run.
scenarios.body: Horses like Obito and Alcaraz, who have demonstrated willingness to settle and finish strongly on soft, find the conditions turning entirely in their favour as the field strings out late; those with questionable soft-ground form fade and leave a clear lane for the resolute stayer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If First Ambition or Lavender Gold steals a decisive early advantage and the prominent pack cancel each other out in pursuit.
scenarios.body: One of the leaders builds an unassailable cushion by the home turn and clings on as tired rivals fail to mount a coordinated challenge; this requires the others to race too keenly chasing fractions and is the least likely outcome given the depth of prominent horses in the field.

watchPoints.text: First Ambition and Lavender Gold will contest the lead — watch the early sectionals closely, as whichever asserts dominance fastest will dictate whether this becomes a true test of stamina or a steadier affair.

Obito is the only horse in the field whose last run was a win on soft ground over the same trip; if Tudhope gets a smooth passage from the rear, he could prove difficult to beat in Scenario A conditions.

Bearish's sole soft-ground run produced a thirteenth-place finish — if conditions are testing rather than merely soft, his chance may be significantly diminished despite his obvious course form on quicker going.

Si Grass and Due To Henry are both genuine prominent types unable to secure their natural position in this field; watch whether either jockey decides to drop them back deliberately or fights for ground early, as the decision will shape how they perform in the straight.

A Major Payne has the strongest course and distance profile in the race with four Goodwood runs over this trip and two wins — if the pace scenario allows him to travel smoothly close to the action rather than being dragged into a battle, his experience at this venue makes him a key shape-dependent runner to monitor.
